name: Azure Disciple
summary: The plains' humanoid visitor: a body authored only from the spirit tier up, so every one of them on the Mortal Plains is an immigrant from a world with a larger law budget. It exists because a mortal-tier world licenses plant and beast life only, which makes a humanoid there not a resident population but a person standing on ground that never expected one - and every dispute over the Cairn Field is a dispute about what to do with them.

name: Cloudshelf Hunter
summary: The sea's apex predator, whose entire population is a function of the kelp and so of the Tidemark season that grows it. It exists because a shelf that can be farmed has to have something that eats what it farms, and life law is written here so the predator is licensed rather than tolerated - which makes the hunt a calendar problem and the water controllable for a window rather than outright.

attributes.season: the Tidemark, when the kelp is thick
attributes.window: the hunt has a season rather than a territory, so the sea is controllable for a period and not otherwise

name: Cloudshelf Kelp
summary: The sea's whole food base: a kelp that grows in the tideline and stops the moment the Tidemark turns against it. It exists because the shelf has to feed whatever lives in it, and a kelp on a written season is the only food source that can be farmed and defended at once - so the shore is worth more than the fish in it, and the tideline is the setting's first genuinely arguable boundary.

attributes.role: the base of the shelf's entire food web
attributes.contested_object: the tideline rather than the open water

name: Gale Pass Swift
summary: The flock that crosses the Gale Pass in the season the gale is worst, occupying the only usable hours of the only crossing for part of the Tidemark. It exists because the pass is scheduled rather than open, so the swift's season is the season nobody wants to cross in anyway - making it a co-holder of the pass who cannot be reasoned with, and capping how absolute any gate there can be.

attributes.season: the worst of the Tidemark, when the gate is shut anyway
attributes.effect: takes the usable hours of the crossing for part of the season
attributes.implication: the pass has a second holder who cannot be bargained with, which caps how absolute any gate can be

name: The Hollow Measure Herd
summary: The plains' one large migratory herd, returning on a cycle nobody on the ground has predicted, and therefore the tier's only moving calendar. It matters because temporal law is written here at 0.5-2.0 with qi at the floor, so the flood is the only cycle available - the return can be waited for but not scheduled, which makes the herd both the tier's famine vector and its calendar.

attributes.trigger: the Widow Run flood, not a season; elemental law is unspent so nothing here is dormant
attributes.what_it_carries: grazing pressure, which is what decides whether herb_common survives the year
attributes.why_it_is_the_tier_calendar: it is the only population on the plains whose arrival date moves the economy

name: Iron Scar Soil
summary: The sterile ground around the Exhausted Seam: spoil that has not moved in four decades because nothing on the plains can carry it away. It exists because spatial law is unspent here, so a mine's exhaustion is not a change in the ground but a permanent addition to it - which makes the Iron Grief a slow disaster whose ruin outlives everyone who remembers the working.

attributes.why_not: elemental and spatial law are unspent here, so nothing in the world carries the spoil away or weathers it
attributes.remediation: none attempted; there is no written process here that would move it

name: Ironhide Bear
summary: The plains' great grazer, whose hide is the only armour the mortal tier can make and whose range follows worked ore. It exists because life law is written here and qi law is spent at the floor of its range - enough for an animal to reach combat power 5 to 50 and to be hunted for a hide that stops a blade. It is also the tier's ecological anchor: it grazes the herb belt that is the only medicine on the plains.

name: Jade Cleft Moss
summary: The cleft's moss: a slow green crust that grows only where the jade seam holds qi and dies back over any cut ground. It matters because jade holds qi and a plant can live on a held gradient, so the moss maps the seam - and because cutting the jade is also grazing it, so a working face is a bare patch regrowing on a schedule nobody on the ridge controls.

attributes.requires: a qi-holding surface, so it marks the seam rather than the cleft
attributes.regrowth: slow and not under any party's control
attributes.use_as_evidence: the moss's boundary is the seam's, which makes it the only honest survey of the cleft

name: The Jade Seam Draft
summary: The qi gradient down the jade seam, which makes the cleft a falling series of thin, hard, increasingly deep workings rather than one large mine. It exists because jade holds qi because nothing about it wants to give it up, so a seam is a gradient to be followed rather than a pocket to be emptied - turning mining into a supply-chain problem and making the pass, not the cleft, the thing worth holding.

attributes.cost_per_step: rises; each stage is deeper and further from the pass
attributes.supply_implication: the pass, not the cleft, is the chokepoint; see geography.gale_pass
attributes.why_it_matters_downstream: no polity can hold the cleft without also paying for the road, which is the cleft's real price

name: The Overlayer Drift
summary: The second layer's ecology: the slow upward movement of surplus law off the Immortal Court's surface, which is what the Overlayer Shelf is made of and what feeds the Ember Ley from below. It exists because ten slots over six groups leaves four duplicates the surface cannot carry, so the excess rises and behaves like weather - making ley and shelf one system, where holding either means negotiating with a supply line you do not own.

attributes.supplied_from: the surface law list's four duplicate imprints
attributes.behaviour: pools upward, drifts, and settles; it behaves like weather rather than like a river
attributes.is_the_shelf: the shelf is where the drift has finished pooling, so shelf and drift are one thing at two stages
attributes.why_it_is_not_a_resource: it is a flow, so holding it means holding the delivery, not the destination

name: Scrub Grazing Pressure
summary: The dynamic that keeps the Bitter Scrub alive and the mortal tier hungry: herb_common is medicine, feed and calories at once. It matters because the scrub regenerates only as fast as it is grazed and the grazers are larger than the households, so the tier's only remedy is also its most contested mouthful, and a bad grazing year is a medical shortage before it is a hunger.

attributes.fencing: impossible at this scale and treated as a trespass wherever it is attempted
attributes.failure_signature: a bad grazing year reads as a medical shortage before it reads as hunger

name: Spirit Herb
summary: The only plant authored into all four world tiers at once, and so the setting's single most portable resource. It exists because life law is one of the three groups a mortal world does write, so the lowest tier can grow a remedy - and the same species is authored at the top tier, which makes it the one good a mortal herbalist and an immortal alchemist can both trade in, and the spine of every economy between the tiers.

name: Storm Elemental
summary: The setting's one authored elemental, licensed only at the immortal and transcendent tiers and reaching combat power 100 to 1000. It exists because elemental law is the group that licenses an elemental and it is unspent in the two lower tiers - so below the Ember Ley this is not a creature that is rare, it is a creature with no lawful existence at all, running at full strength and producing nothing.

name: Third Layer Static
summary: The third layer's ecology, which is the absence of one: nothing there grows, recovers, adapts or is cheap, and the only thing that happens is law being written nine more times. It exists because fifteen imprints over three layers leave more law present than one will can hold, and a system with permanent surplus has no room for anything that must accumulate - including life, so this tier's ecology is a ranking rather than a web.

attributes.recovery: none; a thing that drops here does not come back
attributes.effect: the tier's hierarchy is physical rather than declared, because standing in surplus is the rank
attributes.why_the_tier_is_built: 15 imprints over 3 layers exceed one will, so the ground was assembled by merging; see cosmology.transcendent_world

name: Trial Field Lichen
summary: A grey lichen that colonises worked stone wherever a large quantity of qi has been drawn through it, making it the only reliable marker that a trial has been held. It matters because the trace never washes off, so all four rings are legible from above as pale patches - which makes it a court record nobody can edit, and on the Terrace Ring the mark outlives the argument about what happened.

attributes.grows_on: worked stone where qi has been drawn through in quantity
attributes.why_it_matters: a trial's history becomes legible on the ground rather than in a ledger, so it cannot be edited by whoever lost

name: Vacant Elemental Ground
summary: The ground effect at the two elemental domains where elemental law is unspent: a technique at full strength producing nothing, which is the signature absence leaves rather than weakness. It exists because an unwritten law group has three signatures - no process, no substance, no licensed life form - and an elemental technique needs all three, which is why the Ember and Tide Domains are the setting's most instructive ruins.

attributes.signature: absent, not reduced; the technique reaches full strength and has no substrate
attributes.cost_to_a_practitioner: the realm is reachable and the effect is not
attributes.why_it_is_the_same_shape_twice: both tiers left elemental law unspent, so the same experiment was run at two levels and failed identically

name: Pan Halophile Mat
summary: The salt-tolerant mat that skins the basin's brine and crusts the pan surface, and the setting's only food base that a brine-bearing body can use at all. It matters because it grows to whatever concentration the basin currently holds - so when the chemistry of the brine changes, the mat follows it and a body built to read concentration has nothing left to read, which is a collapse with no visible cause.

provenance.author: w5-linking
basis: abstract-pattern:a resource that exists must belong to an ecosystem that supports it
named-gap: races.saltfolk eat halophilic algae and races.deepsalt is authored as unable to use 'the pan organisms their parent eats'; ecology held no record of either

attributes.for_whom: a body whose taste reads concentration across four orders of dilution
attributes.the_failure_mode: the mat survives a chemistry change and the body does not, so the collapse looks like the mat working normally

name: Ash-Scoured Lichen
summary: The crust that colonises the volcanic belt's ash fans, ash-scoured to grey on the upwind face and black where the fall is fresh. It is the base of the belt's entire food chain because it is the only thing there that fixes stone into something a body can eat, and it matters for a second reason: it records fall thickness, so a quiet decade is legible on the rock years after the arc stops being interesting.

provenance.author: w5-linking
basis: abstract-pattern:a resource that exists must belong to an ecosystem that supports it
named-gap: races.ashwalker is authored as eating 'ash-scoured lichen' and races.ashjackal as thriving on what the belt kills; ecology held no record of either

attributes.processes: stone into protein, which is the only reason the belt has a food chain at all
attributes.records: fall thickness in its own growth, so a quiet decade is legible after the fact
attributes.recovered_by: whoever eats spent ground, and by nothing that hunts

name: Cavern Lumen Fungus
summary: The luminous hyphal mat that skins every wet wall of the deep caverns and emits light rather than receiving it. It matters because it reads a hand on the wall by the pattern of its own response, which is the only way a lightless body navigates, and because its strains do not mix: a host pair must find a matching strain within a year or the colony rejects the child.

provenance.author: w5-linking
basis: abstract-pattern:a resource that exists must belong to an ecosystem that supports it
named-gap: races.lanternfolk is a colony of 'fine luminous hyphae' requiring 'a compatible fungal strain within range' and ecology held no record of the fungus

attributes.light_is_emitted: the colony's own light is useless to it; it reads surfaces by its response to a touch
attributes.strain_rules: strains do not mix, which is why pairing is a rite with a deadline
attributes.dies_above: dry, sunlit or vibrating ground, and to fire inside a season
